subject: FastLedger token surge — reserved capacity not applied / urgent remediation
body:
From: Alice Gomez <alice@fastledger.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: [FastLedger] sudden latency & 429s — reserved bursts not kicking in

Hi Mina / Marissa,

We started seeing a large spike in end-user latency and a wave of 429s this morning across our production cluster (eu-west and us-west). Metrics show a 7x token rate spike starting ~07:45 PDT; our dashboards claim reserved bursts should have added capacity but token processing queues still grew and errors climbed. This is customer-impacting — transaction confirmations are timing out.

We attached a short set of logs and a flamegraph (fastledger_error_trace.zip) and can share more if needed. Can someone confirm whether Redwood applied reserved capacity for our account during the window? If it did, why didn't it absorb the surge? If not, what immediate mitigations exist while we coordinate?

We need an ETA for a fix and something we can communicate to execs here.

Thanks,
Alice Gomez
Head of Platform, FastLedger
alice@fastledger.com

--
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@fastledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [FastLedger] sudden latency & 429s — reserved bursts not kicking in

Alice — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I'm escalating this immediately and looping David (SRE) for diagnostics.

Short answers up front: we will (1) confirm whether reserved capacity was routed correctly; (2) deploy a short-term traffic shaping/fallback to your canary model if we can; (3) authorize an emergency burst of capacity if needed while we fix the root cause.

Immediate asks from FastLedger: 1) Can you confirm whether you initiated any large async job or batch at ~07:40 PDT? 2) Can you share a sample request id that shows a 429 so we can trace it internally?

I will set a 30-min ops bridge and a concurrent executive sync if we can't get the queue depth under control within 45 minutes.

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice@fastledger.com>, ops@fastledger.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [FastLedger] sudden latency & 429s — reserved bursts not kicking in

Quick technical readout from initial triage:
- Observed symptom: token-processing queue for FastLedger tenant spiked and backed into the shared serving scheduler; priority routing to their reserved GPU pool appears to have been delayed by ~3 minutes before we saw spillover to other capacity.
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a sudden token-surge (bot-driven traffic) caused very large KV cache churn and elevated sequence lengths. Our routing policy deferred to short-latency slots but those were saturated and queue-ordering prevented immediate scaling of the dedicated pool. In short: the scheduler honoured reservation claims, but the path to attach warmed KV caches to reserved workers was slower than expected under the surge pattern.

Short-term mitigations deployed (11:12 PDT):
1) Enabled per-tenant request shaping (limit to steady QPS, prioritize confirmed interactive sessions).
2) Redirected non-critical model variants to lower-cost regional capacity to free headroom in the reserved pool.
3) Activated the emergency burst capacity for FastLedger (we have a one-off buffer for SEV-level events).

Impact so far: queue depth reduced ~60% in 20 minutes and 429s dropped to baseline levels for the interactive path. We still see higher tail latency for long sequences; that requires cache-warm strategies (see runbook).

Next steps I recommend:
- Approve a 2-hour priority allocation (move 4 nodes to FastLedger's reserved pool) to give us time to implement a model-fallback and KV pre-warm.
- Run the KV pre-warm job (estimated 18 minutes) for their most common prompt prefixes.
- Post-incident: update scheduler to accelerate hot-attach path for reserved pools and add a fast-fail detector to avoid delayed routing.

Attached: diag-snapshot.png (scheduler timelines + queue traces). Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/gpu-pool-spillover-v1

-David
David Kim
SRE Lead, Runtime Services

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice@fastledger.com>, ops@fastledger.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: FastLedger incident update and asks for exec approval

Team — short update and concrete asks so we can move quickly:

What happened (TL;DR): A fast token surge for FastLedger caused KV-cache churn and temporarily delayed the scheduler hot-attach path to their reserved GPUs. The reservation claim itself was not rejected, but the attach latency allowed queues to grow and user traffic experienced 429s and higher tail latency.

Immediate status: mitigations from David reduced queues by ~60% and restored interactive success rates. We still have elevated tail latency for long sequences.

Asks for exec (Aditya / Marissa):
1) Approve an immediate, one-time emergency burst credit and priority allocation: move 4 reserved nodes to FastLedger for the next 2 hours (estimated cost impact: ~USD 2,400).
2) Approve a short customer message (I drafted below) and a joint exec call if FastLedger wants one.
3) Prioritize a scheduler patch to accelerate hot-attach in the next sprint and authorize a small post-mortem task force (SRE + Runtime + Product) to ship the fix in the coming 2 sprints.

Draft customer message (short):
"Alice — we started a mitigation at 11:12 PDT, redirected non-critical traffic, and authorized emergency burst capacity. Your interactive traffic has returned to normal; we will keep the priority allocation for two hours and follow up with a technical post-mortem and timeline for a permanent fix. Apologies for the disruption. — Mina, Redwood"

Why this needs quick exec support: FastLedger is a strategic account (contract FAST-2027-42) and this is visible to their board. Quick approval prevents churn and preserves our SLA compliance posture.

I'll hold the ops bridge for another 30 minutes and will not scale the allocation down until I hear from either Aditya or Marissa.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
